Jedrzejow
yen-DZHAY-yoof
n. (the Lesser Polish Cistercian abbey of 1140, the first of the order in Poland, burial place of the chronicler Wincenty Kadlubek)
Polish Jedrzejow, Andrew's place, from Jedrzej, Andrew; formerly Morimundus Minor.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Jedrzejow in Lesser Poland was founded in 1140 and settled from Morimond, which made it the first Cistercian house in Poland and the parent of the Polish branch of the order. Its second distinction is a man: Wincenty Kadlubek, bishop of Krakow, resigned his see in 1218, took the habit at Jedrzejow and died there, leaving the Chronica Polonorum, the earliest sustained narrative of the Polish past written by a Pole. The abbey kept his tomb and the chronicle kept the nation's memory. The dictionary records Jedrzejow for that office of remembering, which Scripture treats as a duty rather than an antiquarian taste. The psalmist makes handing on the record a refusal to be silent, “We will not hide them from their children” (Psa 78:4), and the thing to be handed down is measured by its usefulness to those who come after, “that ye may tell it to the generation following” (Psa 48:13). A man who leaves a true account leaves an estate of a kind, “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children” (Pro 13:22), and the contentment proper to such a portion is confessed and not merely felt, “yea, I have a goodly heritage” (Psa 16:6).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines a chronicle as a historical account in order of time; an annal as a year's record of events; an inheritance as an estate derived from an ancestor; memory as the faculty of recollecting; and a monument as anything by which the memory of persons or events is preserved.

expand to see more

CHRONICLE, n. A historical account of facts or events disposed in the order of time.

ANNALS, n. A species of history digested in order of time, or a relation of events in chronological order.

INHERITANCE, n. An estate derived from an ancestor to an heir by succession or in course of law.

MEMORY, n. The faculty of the mind by which it retains the knowledge of past events.

MONUMENT, n. Any thing by which the memory of a person or of an event is preserved or perpetuated.

Key Scripture

Psa 78:4 — "We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of the LORD, and his strength, and his wonderful works that he hath done."

Psa 48:13 — "Mark ye well her bulwarks, consider her palaces; that ye may tell it to the generation following."

Pro 13:22 — "A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just."

Psa 16:6 — "The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places; yea, I have a goodly heritage."

Modern Corruption

Poland's first Cistercian house, 1140, settled from Morimond, burial place of the chronicler Wincenty Kadlubek.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that keeping a true record is a duty laid on the living. Kadlubek resigned a bishopric and spent his last years writing his people's history, and the psalmist frames that labour as a refusal rather than a hobby, “We will not hide them from their children” (Psa 78:4).

The live temptation is to write the past to flatter the house that pays for the ink, which medieval chronicles did constantly and Kadlubek did sometimes. The corrective is the stated audience: a record is made “that ye may tell it to the generation following” (Psa 48:13). An honest account is itself a bequest, “A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children” (Pro 13:22), and the right response to receiving one is gratitude, “The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places” (Psa 16:6).

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew kachad (H3582), to hide, to conceal; Hebrew dor (H1755), a generation; Hebrew nachalah (H5159), an inheritance; Hebrew chebel (H2256), a measuring line, a portion.

expand to see more

Hebrew kachad (H3582) — to hide, to conceal, to withhold; “We will not hide them from their children”, Psalm 78:4.

Hebrew tehillah (H8416) — praise, a song of praise; “the praises of the LORD”, Psalm 78:4.

Hebrew dor (H1755) — a generation, an age; “to the generation following”, Psalm 48:13.

Hebrew nachalah (H5159) — an inheritance, a possession; “A good man leaveth an inheritance”, Proverbs 13:22.

Hebrew chebel (H2256) — a line, a measured portion; “The lines are fallen unto me in pleasant places”, Psalm 16:6.

Usage

"“We will not hide them from their children” (Psa 78:4) — remembering as a refusal, not a taste."

"“that ye may tell it to the generation following” (Psa 48:13) — the audience that keeps a record honest."

"“A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children” (Pro 13:22) — a true account is an estate."
